newsitem.title: VATICAN: Recovering Pope appears before 40,000 pilgrims.
newsitem.headline: Recovering Pope appears before 40,000 pilgrims.

text.p: Pope John Paul, gradually resuming his duties after surgery last month, delivered a weekly address on Sunday to an unusually large crowd of some 40,000 people in St Peter's Square.
Many pilgrims had come for celebrations marking the 76-year-old Pope's 50 years as a priest.
The Pope, who had his appendix removed on October 8, led a mass on Friday in St Peter's Basilica for the anniversary.
The Polish-born Pope appeared in good form as he read his Sunday Angelus, a regular Catholic prayer, from a window of his apartments overlooking the square.
He urged his followers to "rediscover the value of prayer" and held up the liturgy of "our eastern brothers" as inspiration, referring to branches of the Orthodox church.
The Pope has made Christian unity a primary goal of his papacy in the run-up to the year 2000, when he hopes to lead celebrations as Christianity enters its third millennium.
